ai_show_review.summary: Holy Trinity shines despite poor audience recording
ai_show_review.blurb: The show’s highlight is the explosive Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven sequence, with Jerry delivering a lightning‑fast performance. Recording quality is sub‑par audience tape, making most of the set difficult to hear.
ai_show_review.review: On September 26 1969 at the Fillmore East, the Dead unleashed one of their classic “Holy Trinity” moments – a soaring Dark Star that segues into an ecstatic St. Stephen and culminates in the relentless The Eleven. Reviewers repeatedly call Jerry’s guitar work on this Dark Star “lightning‑fast,” “on fire,” and even “the best star ever,” making it a must‑hear for completists despite the tape’s shortcomings. Unfortunately, both available audience recordings suffer from muffled, VBR/OGG artifacts and tape‑reuse glitches that render much of the performance nearly unlistenable. For those willing to brave the audio flaws, this show offers a glimpse into the band’s late‑summer improvisational peak at the Fillmore.

best_recording.reason: Only this tape captures the standout Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven sequence, making it the most valuable despite overall poor sound quality.

key_highlights: Explosive Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven (the “Holy Trinity”)
Jerry’s lightning‑fast guitar work on Dark Star
Performance considered life‑changing by a few listeners despite audio issues

band_performance.Jerry: Lightning‑fast, on fire; many call this Dark Star the best ever.
